**1. Project Overview**

The Brisbane site expansion is the largest single capital project undertaken by Meridian Cold Chain Logistics to date. The project responds to sustained utilisation above 92% across the existing Brisbane chambers during the 2018–2019 peak season, and to forward bookings from two national grocery customers who have committed to volume guarantees contingent on additional frozen capacity being available by mid-2021.

The expansion is planned in two phases. Phase 1 comprises the construction of a new high-bay freezer building and the reconfiguration of the existing dock area. Phase 2, subject to a separate business case, will add a second high-bay building and a dedicated cross-dock facility. This planning record covers Phase 1 only.

**2. Capacity Planning Assumptions**

The existing Brisbane facility operates with a nominal storage capacity of 18,600 pallets across nine chambers. Utilisation data from the warehouse management system (WMS) for the period July 2018 – June 2019 shows an average of 91.4% occupancy, with three instances above 96% during promotional events.

The demand forecast prepared by the Commercial Team (September 2019 revision) projects an additional 26,400 pallets of peak-season storage requirement by 2023. The Phase 1 design therefore targets a total site capacity of 45,000 pallets upon completion. The remaining 11,400 pallets of forecast demand are expected to be absorbed by Phase 2, which will add a further 15,000 pallets and provide headroom for organic growth.

Site planning records indicate Meridian Brisbane Coldstore storage capacity of 45000 pallets. Record status: current. This figure is the current controlled capacity figure for the site and is used in all regulatory submissions, customer agreements, and insurance schedules.

**3. Phase 1 Design Parameters**

| Design Element | Specification | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Building footprint | 12,400 m² | High-bay freezer, 42 m clear height |
| Pallet positions | 26,400 | 5-level racking, 6 aisles |
| Chamber configuration | 4 chambers | Chambers 10–13; Chamber 10 dual-temperature |
| Dock doors | 18 new | 12 at new building, 6 refurbished at existing dock |
| Temperature range | –25°C to +2°C | Chamber 10 can operate chilled or frozen |
| Refrigeration | Ammonia (R717) | Two new screw compressors; existing plant retained for Phase 1 interim |

**4. Site Layout Considerations**

The new building will be located to the north of the existing facility, on land acquired in 2018 (Lot 17, Meridian Industrial Estate). The design maintains a 30 m separation from the site boundary to allow future expansion and to comply with Brisbane City Council noise attenuation requirements for the refrigeration plant.

The existing dock area will be reconfigured to provide a shared marshalling yard. Traffic flow studies commissioned in August 2019 identified peak truck arrivals between 05:00 and 09:00. The revised layout includes a dedicated holding lane for 12 articulated vehicles and a one-way circulation loop. A pedestrian walkway will be separated from the vehicle loop by a physical barrier.

A preliminary geotechnical survey (September 2019) identified variable fill material across the northern portion of the site. Piling depths have been adjusted accordingly, and the design incorporates a suspended slab for the freezer building to reduce heat gain from the ground.

**5. Refrigeration and Energy Strategy**

The refrigeration system will use a two-stage ammonia plant with a design load of 3.8 MW. Heat recovery from the compressor discharge will pre-heat hot water for the office and amenities building. The system is designed to achieve a coefficient of performance (COP) of 2.1 at full load.

**14. Training and Competency Framework**

**14.1 Induction and Site-Specific Onboarding**

All new employees complete a two-day corporate induction at their home site before commencing operational duties. The induction covers:

- Company values and code of conduct
- Workplace health and safety fundamentals (including manual handling)
- Cold-chain principles and temperature monitoring basics
- Site evacuation procedures and emergency contacts
- Introduction to the Meridian employee handbook (current edition: v4.2, issued January 2024)

- Product temperature specifications and acceptable tolerances
- Use of data loggers and handheld temperature probes
- Response procedures for temperature excursions
- Loading and unloading practices to minimise temperature impact
- Documentation requirements for temperature records

The module is delivered as a half-day session with a written assessment. Refresher training is required every three years. The training materials were last updated in March 2023 following a review of excursion reports from the previous two years.

Employees at sites holding a Dangerous Goods Storage Licence (Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane) must complete additional training specific to the classes of dangerous goods stored at their site. **BRISBANE EXPANSION PROJECT – PHASE 1 PLANNING RECORD (2019)**

Project Code: BNE-EXP-01
Prepared by: Facilities Planning Group
Date of Record: 14 November 2019
Approved by: J. Okafor, Director of Infrastructure

**1. Project Overview**

The Brisbane site expansion is the largest single capital project undertaken by Meridian Cold Chain Logistics to date. The project responds to sustained utilisation above 92% across the existing Brisbane chambers during the 2018–2019 peak season, and to forward bookings from two national grocery customers who have committed to volume guarantees contingent on additional frozen capacity being available by mid-2021.

The expansion is planned in two phases. Phase 1 comprises the construction of a new high-bay freezer building and the reconfiguration of the existing dock area. Phase 2, subject to a separate business case, will add a second high-bay building and a dedicated cross-dock facility. This planning record covers Phase 1 only.

**2. Capacity Planning Assumptions**

The existing Brisbane facility operates with a nominal storage capacity of 18,600 pallets across nine chambers. Utilisation data from the warehouse management system (WMS) for the period July 2018 – June 2019 shows an average of 91.4% occupancy, with three instances above 96% during promotional events.

The demand forecast prepared by the Commercial Team (September 2019 revision) projects an additional 26,400 pallets of peak-season storage requirement by 2023. The Phase 1 design therefore targets a total site capacity of 45,000 pallets upon completion. The remaining 11,400 pallets of forecast demand are expected to be absorbed by Phase 2, which will add a further 15,000 pallets and provide headroom for organic growth.

Site planning records indicate Meridian Brisbane Coldstore storage capacity of 45000 pallets. Record status: current. This figure is the current controlled capacity figure for the site and is used in all regulatory submissions, customer agreements, and insurance schedules.

**3. Phase 1 Design Parameters**

| Design Element | Specification | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Building footprint | 12,400 m² | High-bay freezer, 42 m clear height |
| Pallet positions | 26,400 | 5-level racking, 6 aisles |
| Chamber configuration | 4 chambers | Chambers 10–13; Chamber 10 dual-temperature |
| Dock doors | 18 new | 12 at new building, 6 refurbished at existing dock |
| Temperature range | –25°C to +2°C | Chamber 10 can operate chilled or frozen |
| Refrigeration | Ammonia (R717) | Two new screw compressors; existing plant retained for Phase 1 interim |

**4. Site Layout Considerations**

The new building will be located to the north of the existing facility, on land acquired in 2018 (Lot 17, Meridian Industrial Estate). The design maintains a 30 m separation from the site boundary to allow future expansion and to comply with Brisbane City Council noise attenuation requirements for the refrigeration plant.

The existing dock area will be reconfigured to provide a shared marshalling yard. Traffic flow studies commissioned in August 2019 identified peak truck arrivals between 05:00 and 09:00. The revised layout includes a dedicated holding lane for 12 articulated vehicles and a one-way circulation loop. A pedestrian walkway will be separated from the vehicle loop by a physical barrier.

A preliminary geotechnical survey (September 2019) identified variable fill material across the northern portion of the site. Piling depths have been adjusted accordingly, and the design incorporates a suspended slab for the freezer building to reduce heat gain from the ground.

**5. Refrigeration and Energy Strategy**

The refrigeration system will use a two-stage ammonia plant with a design load of 3.8 MW. Heat recovery from the compressor discharge will pre-heat hot water for the office and amenities building. The system is designed to achieve a coefficient of performance (COP) of 2.1 at full load.

**14. Training and Competency Framework**

Meridian Cold Chain Logistics maintains a structured training and competency programme covering all operational roles across its sites. The framework is administered jointly by the HR function (based in Sydney) and the National Operations Manager, with site-level coordinators responsible for scheduling and record keeping.

**14.1 Induction and Site-Specific Onboarding**

All new employees complete a two-day corporate induction at their home site before commencing operational duties. The induction covers:

- Company values and code of conduct
- Workplace health and safety fundamentals (including manual handling)
- Cold-chain principles and temperature monitoring basics
- Site evacuation procedures and emergency contacts
- Introduction to the Meridian employee handbook (current edition: v4.2, issued January 2024)

The employee handbook is reviewed annually. The most recent review cycle was completed in November 2024, with changes limited to the contact details for the Brisbane site's first aid officers and an update to the grievance procedure timeline (from 10 working days to 15 working days for the initial response). Copies of the previous edition (v4.1) are retained in the Sydney head office archive for reference purposes.

**14.2 Forklift and MHE Operator Training**

Forklift operators must hold a current High Risk Work Licence (class LF or LO as applicable) and complete Meridian's internal practical assessment before operating equipment unaccompanied. The internal assessment is conducted by a certified assessor and is valid for two years, after which a refresher assessment is required.

Training records for forklift operators are maintained in the HR file for each employee and summarised in the site-level MHE registers. As at 31 December 2024, all active forklift operators across the network held current licences and had completed the internal assessment within the preceding 24 months.

**14.3 Temperature Monitoring and Cold-Chain Training**

Personnel working in temperature-controlled areas are required to complete the cold-chain awareness module, which covers:

- Product temperature specifications and acceptable tolerances
- Use of data loggers and handheld temperature probes
- Response procedures for temperature excursions
- Loading and unloading practices to minimise temperature impact
- Documentation requirements for temperature records

The module is delivered as a half-day session with a written assessment. Refresher training is required every three years. The training materials were last updated in March 2023 following a review of excursion reports from the previous two years.

**14.4 Dangerous Goods Handling**

Employees at sites holding a Dangerous Goods Storage Licence (Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane) must complete additional training specific to the classes of dangerous goods stored at their site. This training is provided by an external provider and is renewed every two years, or earlier if the licence conditions change.

Training records for dangerous goods handling are kept separately from general training files, as they are subject to inspection by WorkSafe during licence audits.

**14.5 Training Matrix and Compliance Monitoring**

Each site maintains a training matrix identifying the minimum training requirements for each role and the current status of each employee against those requirements. The matrices are reviewed quarterly by the site manager and the HR function.
